<!--
Baseline models B1-B6 of the lean model plan (version 2, 6 October 2026):
research_plan/Model plan — bribe requests, connection delays and costs.md, section "Main text".
B1-B3: log days on the bribe request, adding survey FE / clustering, then controls and sector dummies.
B4: B3 on the cost sample (N_J), so that B3 vs B5 is not a change of sample.
B5: log cost (winsorized deviation from the survey median) with the B3 specification.
B6: selection check, LPMs of pending / denied on the bribe request (all applicants).
Inference: SE clustered by country; wild cluster bootstrap (Webb) for the headline models B3 and B5.
MDEs of B3 and B5 under the table. The coefficients are conditional associations, not causal effects.
-->


## Libraries
```{r,echo=FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)
```

## Loading data

```{r}

## na.strings: empty sector cells must be read as NA, not as an empty category ""
baseline <- read.csv('C:/Users/alexa/Documents/bribery-electricity/data/created-data/wbes_baseline.csv',
                     na.strings = c("", "NA"))

## Survey identifier: one wave per country in this stack, so survey = country-wave = country
baseline <- baseline %>%
  mutate(survey = paste0(country_iso3, "_", wave))

## Tables are written to outputs/baseline-<date>/
out_dir <- paste0("C:/Users/alexa/Documents/bribery-electricity/outputs/baseline-", Sys.Date())
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Samples

```{r}
## --- Samples (model plan, "Samples and baseline specification") ---
## S_A: all applicants in the cleaned file: completed, pending or denied, bribe question (C5) answered yes/no.
##      This is the population for the selection check B6: whether a request is related to the status of the
##      application can only be seen among all applicants, not among completed ones.
## N_D: completed connections (c4 > 0). Days are only observed when the connection was obtained, so every
##      delay model is estimated here.
## N_J: completed connections with a positive cost. Zero costs are already NaN in the cleaning notebook and
##      ERI / MDG / SDN / ZAF have no cost question (c31), so N_J is smaller than N_D for structural reasons.
sample_A <- baseline
sample_D <- sample_A %>% filter(c4 > 0)
sample_J <- sample_D %>% filter(cost_connexion > 0)

cat("S_A:", nrow(sample_A), " | N_D:", nrow(sample_D), " | N_J:", nrow(sample_J), "\n")
cat("Countries  S_A:", n_distinct(sample_A$country_iso3), " | N_D:", n_distinct(sample_D$country_iso3),
    " | N_J:", n_distinct(sample_J$country_iso3), "\n")

## Stop if the samples are not the ones of the model plan (e.g. after a re-export of the data)
if (nrow(sample_A) != 2030) stop("S_A should have 2,030 rows, not ", nrow(sample_A))
if (nrow(sample_D) != 1852) stop("N_D should have 1,852 rows, not ", nrow(sample_D))
if (nrow(sample_J) != 1545) stop("N_J should have 1,545 rows, not ", nrow(sample_J))
```

```{r}
## --- Application status for B6 ---
## Coding of c4 taken from code/feature_engineering/clean_baseline_data.ipynb (markdown note on C4 and the
## sample filter df_applied[df_applied.c4 >= -6]):
##   c4 > 0  = number of days to obtain the connection (completed)
##   c4 = -6 = application still in process (pending)
##   c4 = -5 = application denied
##   c4 = -9 (do not know) is dropped by the notebook, so S_A contains only these three statuses.
sample_A <- sample_A %>%
  mutate(pending = as.integer(c4 == -6),
         denied  = as.integer(c4 == -5))

if (any(!(sample_A$c4 > 0 | sample_A$c4 %in% c(-6, -5)))) stop("Unexpected c4 code in S_A")

table(status = ifelse(sample_A$c4 > 0, "completed", ifelse(sample_A$c4 == -6, "pending", "denied")),
      bribe_request = sample_A$bribe_request)
```

```{r}
## --- Cost without extreme values (frozen decision 2), copied from the heterogeneity Rmd ---
## Costs are in local currency, so extremes are defined relative to the survey median, in logs:
## deviation = log cost - survey median of log cost. The survey median is absorbed by the survey FE anyway,
## so only the deviation matters for the model, and capping it treats a cost 100 times the median the same way
## in every currency.
## The 1st and 99th percentiles of the deviations are computed ONCE, on all N_J firms pooled; deviations outside
## are capped (firms are kept). The two cutoffs are stored as objects: every later subsample (robustness,
## heterogeneity) must reuse them rather than recompute them, otherwise the outcome itself would change with
## the subsample.
sample_J <- sample_J %>%
  group_by(survey) %>%
  mutate(cost_dev = log_cost_connexion - median(log_cost_connexion)) %>%
  ungroup()

dev_p01 <- unname(quantile(sample_J$cost_dev, 0.01))
dev_p99 <- unname(quantile(sample_J$cost_dev, 0.99))

sample_J <- sample_J %>%
  mutate(log_cost_w = log_cost_connexion - cost_dev + pmin(pmax(cost_dev, dev_p01), dev_p99))

cat("Cutoffs of the deviation from the survey median (log points): p1 =", round(dev_p01, 3),
    " | p99 =", round(dev_p99, 3), "\n")
cat("Firms winsorized:", sum(abs(sample_J$log_cost_w - sample_J$log_cost_connexion) > 1e-9), "\n")
```

```{r}
## Baseline controls X (5 October 2026): X^core frozen on 4 October + capital city.
## Sector enters separately, as dummies: i(sector, ref = "Trade_Hospitality") in each formula below.
## log_age = log(1 + age), as built in code/feature_engineering/clean_baseline_data.ipynb.
ctrl_core <- c("log_employment", "log_age", "new_establishment", "foreign_owned", "government_owned",
               "in_multi_establishment", "shareholding", "exporter", "top_manager_female", "capital_city")
```

## Missing values

Rows with a missing value in any model variable are dropped by `feols`. They are counted here and in every
model below, so that no row disappears silently.

```{r}
## --- Missing values in the model variables, by sample ---
missing_table <- data.frame(
  variable = c("log_days", "log_cost_w", "bribe_request", ctrl_core, "sector"),
  S_A = NA, N_D = NA, N_J = NA
)
for (i in 1:nrow(missing_table)) {
  v <- missing_table$variable[i]
  missing_table$S_A[i] <- if (v %in% names(sample_A)) sum(is.na(sample_A[[v]])) else NA
  missing_table$N_D[i] <- if (v %in% names(sample_D)) sum(is.na(sample_D[[v]])) else NA
  missing_table$N_J[i] <- sum(is.na(sample_J[[v]]))
}
missing_table %>% filter(S_A > 0 | N_D > 0 | N_J > 0)
```

```{r}
## --- Rows of the sample not used by a model ---
## fixest drops a row when any variable of the formula is missing. The count of dropped rows is compared with
## the number of incomplete rows on these variables: a drop for any other reason (e.g. a removed fixed effect)
## stops the script instead of passing unnoticed. The IDs of the dropped firms are printed.
dropped_rows <- function(model, data, vars, label) {
  data <- as.data.frame(data)
  n_dropped <- nrow(data) - nobs(model)
  incomplete <- !complete.cases(data[, vars])
  if (n_dropped != sum(incomplete)) stop(label, ": rows dropped for a reason other than missing values")
  cat(label, ": sample", nrow(data), "| used", nobs(model), "| dropped for missing values", n_dropped,
      if (n_dropped > 0) paste0("(idstd: ", paste(data$idstd[incomplete], collapse = ", "), ")"), "\n")
  n_dropped
}

## Number of countries (clusters) in the estimation sample of a model
n_clusters <- function(model, data) {
  length(unique(as.data.frame(data)$country_iso3[obs(model)]))
}
```


## Baseline models B1-B5

```{r}
## --- B1: raw association, log days on the bribe request, N_D ---
## No fixed effects and no controls: the pooled difference in log days between requesters and non-requesters.
## It is the reference point the other columns move away from. HC1 (heteroskedasticity-robust) SE, as in the
## plan: B1 shows the naive precision; B2 shows how much survey FE and clustering change both the estimate
## and its precision.
b1 <- feols(
  log_days ~ bribe_request,
  vcov = "hetero",
  data = sample_D
)
b1
```

```{r}
## --- B2: + survey fixed effects, SE clustered by country, N_D ---
## Survey FE: delays, utilities, procedures, questionnaire versions and survey years differ across surveys,
## and so does the share of firms reporting a request. With survey FE the coefficient compares requesters with
## non-requesters of the same survey only; surveys without requesters contribute nothing to it.
## Clustering by country: residuals are correlated within a country (same utility and regulator, same survey
## design and fieldwork), and so are the requests. With one wave per country, survey = country, so the survey
## FE are nested in the clusters. 48 clusters.
b2 <- feols(
  log_days ~ bribe_request
  | survey,
  cluster = ~country_iso3,
  data = sample_D
)
b2
```

```{r}
## --- B3 (headline delay model): + controls X + sector dummies, survey FE, clustered by country, N_D ---
## Controls: firm characteristics that can affect both exposure to requests and the time to connect
## (size, age, ownership, multi-establishment, legal form, exporter, manager gender, capital city).
## Sector as dummies, not as a fixed effect (author decision, 5 October 2026): the bribe coefficient is
## identical with sector FE, but the dummies keep the sector differences visible. Reference category
## Trade_Hospitality, the largest group; the reference does not change the bribe coefficient.
## The one firm without a resolved sector (Sudan) has sector = NA and is dropped by i(sector); it is
## reported below with the other missing values, not assigned to a category.
## B3 also drops the firms with missing controls, so B2 -> B3 changes the specification and the sample by a
## few rows (counts below).
b3 <- feols(
  log_days ~ bribe_request + log_employment + log_age + new_establishment + foreign_owned +
    government_owned + in_multi_establishment + shareholding + exporter + top_manager_female + capital_city +
    i(sector, ref = "Trade_Hospitality")
  | survey,
  cluster = ~country_iso3,
  data = sample_D
)
b3
```

```{r}
## --- B4: B3 on N_J (log days, completed connections with a positive cost) ---
## Same specification as B3, on the cost sample. B3 vs B4 shows how much the delay coefficient moves when the
## sample is restricted to firms with a cost; B4 vs B5 then compares delay and cost on the same firms.
b4 <- feols(
  log_days ~ bribe_request + log_employment + log_age + new_establishment + foreign_owned +
    government_owned + in_multi_establishment + shareholding + exporter + top_manager_female + capital_city +
    i(sector, ref = "Trade_Hospitality")
  | survey,
  cluster = ~country_iso3,
  data = sample_J
)
b4
```

```{r}
## --- B5 (headline cost model): log cost (winsorized), B3 specification, N_J ---
## Cost helps interpret the delay result: a request could buy speed (higher cost, shorter delay) or be extracted
## with no change in speed. The cost outcome is the winsorized log-cost deviation built above.
## The questionnaire does not say whether the reported cost (C31) includes informal payments.
b5 <- feols(
  log_cost_w ~ bribe_request + log_employment + log_age + new_establishment + foreign_owned +
    government_owned + in_multi_establishment + shareholding + exporter + top_manager_female + capital_city +
    i(sector, ref = "Trade_Hospitality")
  | survey,
  cluster = ~country_iso3,
  data = sample_J
)
b5
```

```{r}
## --- Rows dropped for missing values, every model ---
vars_b3 <- c("log_days", "bribe_request", ctrl_core, "sector", "survey", "country_iso3")
vars_b5 <- c("log_cost_w", "bribe_request", ctrl_core, "sector", "survey", "country_iso3")

dropped <- c(
  B1 = dropped_rows(b1, sample_D, c("log_days", "bribe_request"), "B1"),
  B2 = dropped_rows(b2, sample_D, c("log_days", "bribe_request", "survey", "country_iso3"), "B2"),
  B3 = dropped_rows(b3, sample_D, vars_b3, "B3"),
  B4 = dropped_rows(b4, sample_J, vars_b3, "B4"),
  B5 = dropped_rows(b5, sample_J, vars_b5, "B5")
)
```


## Wild cluster bootstrap (B3, B5)

With 44-48 countries of very unequal size (a few surveys carry much of the identifying variation: about 19
effective clusters in the stage-1 EDA), the clustered t-test can reject too often. The wild cluster bootstrap
of the t-statistic has much better size in this setting (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2008; MacKinnon and Webb
2017).

- **Restricted (null imposed):** the bootstrap samples are generated under H0, which gives more reliable
  p-values than the unrestricted version.
- **Webb weights:** six values (±√1.5, ±1, ±√0.5) drawn per country. Rademacher (±1) gives only 2^G distinct
  samples and is less reliable with unbalanced clusters (Webb 2023).
- **9,999 draws, fixed seed:** (B + 1) × 0.05 is an integer, and the simulation error of a p-value near 0.05
  is about 0.002. The same draws are used for every hypothesis tested, so the CI is stable.
- **95% CI by test inversion:** the set of values beta0 that the bootstrap test does not reject at 5%, so the
  CI and the p-value always agree.

The bootstrap is written out step by step (the package fwildclusterboot is no longer on CRAN). It is the
restricted bootstrap of the earlier baseline Rmd, with one change for speed: instead of re-estimating the model
for each draw, the model is projected once on the controls and fixed effects (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell), so that
each draw only needs country sums (the algorithm of Roodman et al. 2019). The check at the end of this section
re-estimates the first draws with `feols`, as in the earlier Rmd, and must give the same t-statistics.

```{r}
## --- Function: wild cluster restricted bootstrap with Webb weights, for the bribe-request coefficient ---
wild_bootstrap_webb <- function(model, data, outcome, B = 9999, seed = 20261006, level = 0.95) {

  ## Estimation sample of the model (the rows fixest used)
  d <- as.data.frame(data)[obs(model), ]
  y <- d[[outcome]]
  D <- d$bribe_request

  ## Every other regressor of B3 / B5: controls, sector dummies and survey dummies (= survey FE)
  Z <- model.matrix(as.formula(paste0(
    "~ ", paste(ctrl_core, collapse = " + "),
    " + relevel(factor(sector), ref = 'Trade_Hospitality') + factor(survey)")), data = d)
  qrZ <- qr(Z)

  ## Frisch-Waugh-Lovell: y and D net of Z. The bribe coefficient is sum(D_t * y_t) / sum(D_t^2)
  y_t <- qr.resid(qrZ, y)
  D_t <- qr.resid(qrZ, D)
  SDD <- sum(D_t^2)
  beta_hat <- sum(D_t * y_t) / SDD
  if (abs(beta_hat - coef(model)["bribe_request"]) > 1e-8) stop("FWL coefficient differs from fixest")

  ## Countries
  cl <- d$country_iso3
  clusters <- sort(unique(cl))
  G <- length(clusters)
  q <- tapply(D_t^2, cl, sum)[clusters]           # country sums of D_t^2

  ## Clustered SE of the model. Computed here without small-sample correction (CR0), then scaled by fixest's
  ## correction, so that every t below is exactly fixest's t. The factor is the same in the original and in
  ## every bootstrap draw, so it does not change the p-value.
  score <- tapply(D_t * (y_t - beta_hat * D_t), cl, sum)[clusters]
  se_cr0 <- sqrt(sum(score^2)) / SDD
  se_model <- unname(se(model)["bribe_request"])
  ssc_factor <- (se_model / se_cr0)^2

  ## Webb weights: one per country and draw, drawn once and reused for every beta0
  set.seed(seed)
  webb <- c(-sqrt(1.5), -1, -sqrt(.5), sqrt(.5), 1, sqrt(1.5))
  V <- matrix(sample(webb, G * B, replace = TRUE), nrow = G, ncol = B)

  ## Bootstrap t-statistics under H0: beta = beta0
  bootstrap_t <- function(beta0) {
    ## Restricted model: y - beta0 * D on Z. After FWL its residuals are u_r = y_t - beta0 * D_t
    u_r <- y_t - beta0 * D_t
    ## Bootstrap outcome y* = restricted fit + beta0 * D + u_r * v_country. Net of Z it is
    ## beta0 * D_t + sum over countries h of v_h * M_Z(u_r * 1{country h}).
    ## K[g, h] = sum over firms of country g of D_t * M_Z(u_r * 1{country h}): computed once per beta0.
    K <- matrix(0, G, G)
    for (h in 1:G) {
      e_h <- qr.resid(qrZ, u_r * (cl == clusters[h]))
      K[, h] <- tapply(D_t * e_h, cl, sum)[clusters]
    }
    t_star <- numeric(B)
    for (b in 1:B) {
      Kv <- as.numeric(K %*% V[, b])
      delta <- sum(Kv) / SDD                      # beta* - beta0
      score_star <- Kv - q * delta                # country scores with the unrestricted bootstrap residuals
      t_star[b] <- delta / (sqrt(ssc_factor * sum(score_star^2)) / SDD)
    }
    t_star
  }

  ## Symmetric p-value: share of bootstrap |t*| at least as large as the observed |t|
  p_value <- function(beta0) {
    t_obs <- (beta_hat - beta0) / se_model
    mean(abs(bootstrap_t(beta0)) >= abs(t_obs))
  }

  ## CI: beta0 where the p-value crosses 1 - level, on each side of beta_hat (p = 1 at beta_hat)
  width <- 10 * se_model
  if (p_value(beta_hat - width) >= 1 - level | p_value(beta_hat + width) >= 1 - level) stop("CI search interval too narrow")
  ci_low  <- uniroot(function(b0) p_value(b0) - (1 - level), c(beta_hat - width, beta_hat), tol = 1e-6)$root
  ci_high <- uniroot(function(b0) p_value(b0) - (1 - level), c(beta_hat, beta_hat + width), tol = 1e-6)$root

  list(beta = beta_hat, se = se_model, t = beta_hat / se_model, p_value = p_value(0),
       ci_low = ci_low, ci_high = ci_high, G = G, B = B,
       t_star_0 = bootstrap_t(0), V = V, clusters = clusters)
}
```

```{r}
boot_b3 <- wild_bootstrap_webb(b3, sample_D, "log_days")
boot_b5 <- wild_bootstrap_webb(b5, sample_J, "log_cost_w")

data.frame(model = c("B3 log days, N_D", "B5 log cost (winsorized), N_J"),
           beta  = c(boot_b3$beta, boot_b5$beta),
           se    = c(boot_b3$se, boot_b5$se),
           p_clustered = c(pvalue(b3)["bribe_request"], pvalue(b5)["bribe_request"]),
           p_bootstrap = c(boot_b3$p_value, boot_b5$p_value),
           ci_low  = c(boot_b3$ci_low, boot_b5$ci_low),
           ci_high = c(boot_b3$ci_high, boot_b5$ci_high),
           clusters = c(boot_b3$G, boot_b5$G)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
```

```{r}
## --- Check: the first 20 bootstrap draws of B3, re-estimated directly with feols ---
## As in the earlier baseline Rmd: restricted model without the bribe request (H0: beta = 0), then
## y* = fitted + residual * Webb weight of the country, and the full model re-estimated on y*.
d_check <- sample_D[obs(b3), ]
m0 <- feols(
  log_days ~ log_employment + log_age + new_establishment + foreign_owned +
    government_owned + in_multi_establishment + shareholding + exporter + top_manager_female + capital_city +
    i(sector, ref = "Trade_Hospitality")
  | survey,
  data = d_check
)
yhat0 <- predict(m0)
u0    <- resid(m0)

t_check <- numeric(20)
for (b in 1:20) {
  w_by_cluster <- boot_b3$V[, b]
  names(w_by_cluster) <- boot_b3$clusters
  d_check$y_star <- yhat0 + u0 * w_by_cluster[d_check$country_iso3]
  m_b <- feols(
    y_star ~ bribe_request + log_employment + log_age + new_establishment + foreign_owned +
      government_owned + in_multi_establishment + shareholding + exporter + top_manager_female + capital_city +
      i(sector, ref = "Trade_Hospitality")
    | survey,
    cluster = ~country_iso3,
    data = d_check
  )
  t_check[b] <- tstat(m_b)["bribe_request"]
}
cat("Largest difference in t*, feols vs bootstrap function (first 20 draws):",
    max(abs(t_check - boot_b3$t_star_0[1:20])), "\n")
if (max(abs(t_check - boot_b3$t_star_0[1:20])) > 1e-6) stop("Bootstrap function does not reproduce feols")
```


## Baseline table

```{r}
## --- One table for B1-B5: beta, SE (HC1 in B1, clustered by country in B2-B5), bootstrap p-value and CI,
## N, number of clusters, rows dropped for missing values ---
baseline_table <- etable(
  b1, b2, b3, b4, b5,
  headers = c("B1", "B2", "B3", "B4", "B5"),
  keep = "%bribe_request",
  dict = c(bribe_request = "Bribe request", log_days = "log days", log_cost_w = "log cost (winsorized)",
           survey = "Survey"),
  fitstat = ~ n,
  extralines = list(
    "Sample" = c("N_D", "N_D", "N_D", "N_J", "N_J"),
    "Controls and sector dummies" = c("No", "No", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"),
    "Standard errors" = c("HC1", "Clustered", "Clustered", "Clustered", "Clustered"),
    "Clusters (countries)" = c("", n_clusters(b2, sample_D), n_clusters(b3, sample_D),
                               n_clusters(b4, sample_J), n_clusters(b5, sample_J)),
    "Wild cluster bootstrap p (Webb)" = c("", "", sprintf("%.3f", boot_b3$p_value), "",
                                          sprintf("%.3f", boot_b5$p_value)),
    "Bootstrap 95% CI" = c("", "", sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", boot_b3$ci_low, boot_b3$ci_high), "",
                           sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", boot_b5$ci_low, boot_b5$ci_high)),
    "Dropped for missing values" = dropped
  )
)
baseline_table

write.csv(baseline_table, paste0(out_dir, "/baseline_table_B1_B5.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
## --- Full coefficient table for B1-B5 (appendix version of the baseline table) ---
## The table above shows only the bribe request. This export keeps every coefficient: the request, the controls
## and the sector dummies (reference Trade_Hospitality, so each sector coefficient is the difference from it).
## SE and p-values are those of each model as estimated: HC1 in B1, clustered by country in B2-B5 (fixest's
## default small-sample correction and t with G - 1 df). B1 also has an intercept; the survey FE of B2-B5 are not
## coefficients and are not listed. N and the number of clusters are repeated on every row of a model so that the
## file can be filtered by model; clusters is NA for B1, which is not clustered.
full_coefficients <- data.frame()
for (name in c("B1", "B2", "B3", "B4", "B5")) {
  m <- list(B1 = b1, B2 = b2, B3 = b3, B4 = b4, B5 = b5)[[name]]
  m_data <- if (name %in% c("B1", "B2", "B3")) sample_D else sample_J
  ct <- as.data.frame(coeftable(m))
  full_coefficients <- bind_rows(full_coefficients, data.frame(
    model = name,
    outcome = as.character(formula(m)[[2]]),
    term = rownames(ct),
    beta = ct[, "Estimate"],
    se = ct[, "Std. Error"],
    p_value = ct[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
    se_type = if (name == "B1") "HC1" else "clustered by country",
    n = nobs(m),
    clusters = if (name == "B1") NA else n_clusters(m, m_data)
  ))
}
full_coefficients %>% mutate(across(c(beta, se, p_value), ~ round(.x, 4)))

write.csv(full_coefficients, paste0(out_dir, "/baseline_full_coefficients_B1_B5.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Minimum detectable effects (B3, B5)

```{r}
## --- MDE: smallest true association the design detects with 80% power in a two-sided 5% test ---
## MDE = (t_{0.975, G-1} + t_{0.80, G-1}) x clustered SE. With clustered SE the number of countries G, not the
## number of firms, sets the degrees of freedom. The MDE uses only the SE, not the estimated beta: it describes
## the precision of the design, it is not an after-the-fact power calculation for the observed estimate.
## The outcomes are in logs, so the MDE in log points is converted to a percentage change: exp(MDE) - 1 for an
## increase, exp(-MDE) - 1 for a decrease.
mde_table <- data.frame()
for (spec in list(list(name = "B3 log days, N_D", model = b3, data = sample_D),
                  list(name = "B5 log cost (winsorized), N_J", model = b5, data = sample_J))) {
  G <- n_clusters(spec$model, spec$data)
  se_b <- unname(se(spec$model)["bribe_request"])
  mde <- (qt(0.975, G - 1) + qt(0.80, G - 1)) * se_b
  mde_table <- bind_rows(mde_table, data.frame(
    model = spec$name, clusters = G, se_clustered = se_b,
    mde_log_points = mde,
    mde_pct_increase = 100 * (exp(mde) - 1),
    mde_pct_decrease = 100 * (exp(-mde) - 1)
  ))
}
mde_table %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

write.csv(mde_table, paste0(out_dir, "/mde_B3_B5.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```


## Selection: B6

If a request changed the chance that an application is completed (rather than pending or denied), the delay
models on completed connections would compare selected groups. B6 checks this directly.

```{r}
## --- B6: LPMs of 1{pending} and 1{denied} on the bribe request, survey FE, clustered by country, S_A ---
## Linear probability models, not logit: with survey FE and few denials (23 firms), a logit drops every survey
## without a denial and suffers from the incidental-parameter problem; the LPM keeps all applicants and its
## coefficient is directly the difference in probability (percentage points / 100).
## No controls, as in the plan: the question is whether the status of requesters and non-requesters of the same
## survey differs, not why.
b6_pending <- feols(
  pending ~ bribe_request
  | survey,
  cluster = ~country_iso3,
  data = sample_A
)

b6_denied <- feols(
  denied ~ bribe_request
  | survey,
  cluster = ~country_iso3,
  data = sample_A
)

dropped_b6 <- c(
  pending = dropped_rows(b6_pending, sample_A, c("pending", "bribe_request", "survey", "country_iso3"), "B6 pending"),
  denied  = dropped_rows(b6_denied,  sample_A, c("denied", "bribe_request", "survey", "country_iso3"), "B6 denied")
)

selection_table <- etable(
  b6_pending, b6_denied,
  headers = c("B6 pending", "B6 denied"),
  keep = "%bribe_request",
  dict = c(bribe_request = "Bribe request", survey = "Survey"),
  fitstat = ~ n + my,
  extralines = list(
    "Sample" = c("S_A", "S_A"),
    "Clusters (countries)" = c(n_clusters(b6_pending, sample_A), n_clusters(b6_denied, sample_A)),
    "Dropped for missing values" = dropped_b6
  )
)
selection_table

write.csv(selection_table, paste0(out_dir, "/selection_table_B6.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```


## Summary of the coefficients

```{r}
## --- Bribe-request coefficient in every model ---
models <- list(B1 = b1, B2 = b2, B3 = b3, B4 = b4, B5 = b5, "B6 pending" = b6_pending, "B6 denied" = b6_denied)
summary_table <- data.frame()
for (name in names(models)) {
  m <- models[[name]]
  summary_table <- bind_rows(summary_table, data.frame(
    model = name,
    beta = unname(coef(m)["bribe_request"]),
    se = unname(se(m)["bribe_request"]),
    p_value = unname(pvalue(m)["bribe_request"]),
    n = nobs(m)
  ))
}
summary_table %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))

write.csv(summary_table, paste0(out_dir, "/coefficients_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
